newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mainly lower in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mainly lower in dull trading.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mostly lower on Monday, pressured by chart-driven local and speculative selling, dealers said.

"It is deteriorating technically," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "It needs a boost and nothing is likely to occur until mid-September, when the weather gets cold and demand picks up for mild arabicas. Roasters have enough coffee for now."
The benchmark September contract sunk to a intraday low of 156.00 cents per lb, before scattered short-covering and light industry-linked buying stemmed the downslide, traders said.
By the close, September stood at 158.85 cents, down 5.45 cents on the day. The back months closed 4.00 to 6.00 lower.
Spot July, which expired at 1230 EDT today, ended 3.20 cents higher, at 195.70 cents, which stretched the July/September switch to 36.85 cents compared with 28.20 cents at the close on Friday.
The September/December switch, meanwhile, shrank to 12.90 cents from 14.20 cents.

Coffee prices fell at the outset, despite higher pre-opening expections. Downward momentum accelerated after September broke through chart support at 160.00 and 158.00 cents, touching off commission house sell-stops.
But turnover on the day was impressive, at an estimated 5,796 lots, and traders said the market remained in the summer doldrums.
"It's quiet," said one trader. "Volume is light, interest is thin and open interest remains relatively low. There is no news to prompt anyone to do anything significant."
Total open interest as of Friday stood at 21,900 lots, down 60 lots from the previous session.
Traders said frost-free weather in top-producer Brazil and the steady build-up of CSCE certified coffee stocks continued to weigh on setiment.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported that certified coffee inventories rose by 6,257 60-kg bags as of July 18, to 86,849 bags. An additional 6,340 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that 5,680 bags of coffee were graded and only 2,332 bags had passed exchange approval.
Technically, Refco's Prendergast said the September contract could work its way down to 134.00 cents before demand for new-crop coffees drove prices higher.
In the near-term, traders said 156.00-155.00 cents was seen as September support, followed by 152.00 and 150.00. Resistance was pegged at 160.00 cents.
